target.title: fix(crabbox): preserve UTF-16 boundaries in CLI failure detail truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Crabbox worker error details contain malformed text when a command's stderr has emoji at the 512-character truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

`commandDetail()` replaced raw `.slice(0, MAX_ERROR_DETAIL_CHARS)` with the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from the public plugin SDK barrel. The `.replace(/\s+/gu, " ")` whitespace compression runs before truncation, making the content more dense — which increases the likelihood that non-ASCII characters (emoji in test output, script diagnostics) land on the 512 boundary. The existing code-unit limit and message format remain unchanged; this only backs a cut up to avoid splitting an emoji surrogate pair.

## User Impact

Crabbox worker CLI error messages (warmup/inspect/stop failures) remain well-formed when the remote command output contains long emoji-containing diagnostic text.

## Evidence

### Regression test proving the exact boundary cut (exercises real `testing.commandDetail`)

The test constructs 511 ASCII `x` chars + `😀after`. The emoji surrogate pair spans indices [511, 512]. Current main's raw `.slice(0, 512)` keeps only the high surrogate (U+D83D) while dropping the low surrogate (U+DE00) — the test **fails** on current main. The fixed path uses `truncateUtf16Safe(compressed, 512)` which detects the split pair and backs up to index 511.

### Terminal behavior proof (before vs. after, live Node.js output)

```
=== PR #104612 Live Terminal Proof ===

Input: 511 'x' + emoji + 'after'
  stderr[511]=0xd83d (HIGH surrogate)
  stderr[512]=0xde00 (LOW surrogate)

--- BEFORE fix (current main) ---
  output: ": x...x\ud83d"
  length: 514 code units
  LONE SURROGATE at index 513: 0xd83d ← MALFORMED

--- AFTER fix (truncateUtf16Safe) ---
  output: ": x...x"
  length: 513 code units
  ✅ No lone surrogates — well-formed UTF-16
```

### Test suite
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts -t "preserves well-formed UTF-16"
 ✓ |extensions| crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts > preserves well-formed UTF-16 when CLI failure detail reaches the boundary limit

      Tests  1 passed | 45 skipped (46)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts
 ✓ 46/46 passed
```

### Lint
```
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts
✓ clean
```

target.title: fix(gateway): keep worker SSH tunnel stderr tails UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker SSH tunnel failure details keep a rolling stderr/stdout tail with raw UTF-16 `.slice(-4096)` before `processError()` embeds them in the operator-facing `Error`. When remote diagnostic text has an emoji or other non-BMP character exactly at the left edge of that retained window, the thrown message can start with a lone low surrogate (often rendered as U+FFFD).

This hits the production `createWorkerSshRunner()` path used by `createWorkerTunnelManager` when an SSH tunnel child exits before the ready marker.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` through a small `appendBoundedDiagnosticTail` helper, matching sibling worker-environments truncation in `bootstrap.ts` / `service.ts` and the bounded stderr-tail pattern used by file-transfer. Keep the 4096-unit cap and redaction/whitespace folding in `processError()` unchanged; only the rolling buffer retention becomes surrogate-safe.

This is a display-layer root-cause fix for the failure detail string. It does not change SSH forwarding, ready-marker detection semantics for ASCII markers, reconnect/backoff, or success paths.

## User Impact

**Before:** A worker SSH tunnel failure whose remote stderr crossed the 4096-unit rolling window on an emoji could show a corrupted leading character in the Error message.

**After:** The same failure detail drops the incomplete surrogate at the window edge, so operators get a well-formed diagnostic string.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/gateway/worker-environments/tunnel.ts` (`createWorkerSshRunner` stdout/stderr ring buffer)
- Regression: `src/gateway/worker-environments/tunnel.test.ts` → `keeps SSH tunnel failure stderr on a valid UTF-16 boundary`

target.title: fix: preserve tool-result text across media fallback and context pressure
target.body:
Refs #99241

## What Problem This Solves

This PR covers the two interacting model-visible failure stages reported in #99241:

1. Provider serializers could turn an empty text-only tool result into `(see attached image)`, masking upstream text loss as a media result.
2. Under aggregate tool-result pressure, recovery could reduce or clear a freshly completed result before provider dispatch whenever runtime context, steering, or a follow-up message made that result non-trailing.

The July 9 report on this PR was correct for the earlier head: the provider/media patch removed the placeholder symptom but did not stop prompt projection from emptying fresh text. This updated head fixes both stages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier beta fixes were important but incomplete:

- `v2026.7.1-beta.2` contains #97742 and #98955. They preserve structured text and protect the ordinary syntactically trailing fresh-result batch.
- That protection is trailing-only. A new result followed by runtime context, steering, or follow-up input is still a reachable non-trailing fresh result and could be selected before frozen history.
- The beta.3 line adds #100077 (budget scaling / compaction pressure) and #100272 (runtime-context carrier placement). Those mitigate pressure or change the tail shape, but neither establishes a general projection-freshness recovery invariant.

This update adopts the general fresh-projection invariant proposed in #99524, with credit to @snowzlmbot, and carries forward this PR's runtime-context regression coverage on current `main`.

In aggregate recovery, an unfrozen projection that appears after a frozen baseline is treated as fresh. Recovery now reduces ordinary eligible history first, then frozen history, and only then fresh non-trailing results. The existing trailing batch remains fully protected. If historical reductions cannot satisfy the hard cap, fresh results remain eligible as the final fallback, so the cap is still enforced.

For provider serialization, a new internal media-only fallback helper prevents empty text-only results from becoming image placeholders. The exported `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` behavior remains identical to current `main`, preserving its public Plugin SDK contract for mixed text/media callers.

## User Impact

Long-lived sessions with heavy `exec`, `read`, browser, or other tool traffic should keep the newest tool output model-readable across runtime-context, steering, and follow-up boundaries while older projected history is reduced first.

Media-only results retain a descriptive placeholder. Mixed text/media results preserve explicit text. No config change, migration, or new runtime option is required.

## Evidence

### Reproduction and focused coverage

- The live dist instrumentation in #99241 showed a 234-character fresh result selected as the only eligible entry, reduced to 69 characters, then cleared while 256,138 frozen characters remained.
- New regressions cover 234-character and 4,000-character sentinels followed by runtime-context, steering, and queued follow-up messages.
- A hard-cap regression proves fresh text is eventually reduced when frozen history alone cannot satisfy the budget.
- The existing real `convertToLlm` boundary regression still proves runtime-context carrier metadata survives provider conversion.

### Automated validation

- Focused provider, transport, serializer, and aggregate-truncation suite:
  - 10 files across 3 Vitest shards
  - 792 tests passed after the final merge from `upstream/main`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <15 changed files>`: passed.
- `oxfmt --check <15 changed files>`: passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Clean-checkout build:
  - `OPENCLAW_BUILD_ALL_NO_PNPM=1 OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 node scripts/build-all.mjs gatewayWatch`
  - passed.

### Real Gateway / model proof

A clean checkout containing only current OpenClaw plus this PR patch was run through a real local Gateway with `deepseek-v4-flash` and a 128K context window:

- 40 consecutive real `exec` tool calls in one session.
- 272,000 total characters of tool-result text.
- 40/40 unique sentinels were read and acknowledged by the model, from `H01` through `H40`.
- 14 compaction entries occurred; prompt usage crossed pressure and compacted during the run without losing the fresh sentinel.

This is direct Gateway/provider long-session proof. Browser UI proof is not included in this update.

### Codex autoreview

Repository autoreview was run repeatedly with Codex (`gpt-5.5`, high reasoning):

- One accepted finding identified a mixed text/media regression risk; the implementation was changed to use a non-exported media-only serializer helper.
- A later public-helper finding was rejected after direct comparison with `upstream/main`: the exported helper is unchanged, and the internal helper is not exported through the Plugin SDK.
- No accepted or actionable findings remain.

AI-assisted: reproduction analysis, implementation, validation, and final review were performed with Codex.

target.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk
target.body:
Closes [#89200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89200)

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment's session store.

## What Problem This Solves

Session trajectory artifacts (`.trajectory.jsonl` + `.trajectory-path.json`) were handled inconsistently, and destructively, across the session lifecycle:

1. **Delete** (dashboard / `sessions.delete` RPC) archived the transcript but left the trajectory pair orphaned on disk forever (the original [#89200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89200) defect).
2. **Reset paths** either deleted the trajectory outright (destroying the forensic tool-call record, flagged as a P1 by the automated review on this PR) or left it at its live name to be misclassified later.
3. The **typed `/new` and `/reset`** commands (and the implicit daily/idle rollover) went through a code path with no trajectory handling at all, so fixes applied to the other reset doors never reached the path users actually type.

## What This Change Does

One consistent model: **trajectory artifacts shadow their transcript**. Whenever a session's transcript is archived with a `.reset.<ts>` or `.deleted.<ts>` suffix, the trajectory runtime file and pointer are renamed with the byte-identical suffix in the same operation (shared `nowMs`), never unlinked:

- A `TrajectoryArtifactDisposal` union threads the disposal mode through the cleanup helpers: `{ mode: "tombstone", reason, nowMs }` for user-visible lifecycle events, with rename-in-place semantics under the same `withTrajectoryPathLock` retire turn.
- All three lifecycle doors are coupled: `deleteSessionEntryLifecycle` (delete), `resetSessionEntryLifecycle` (dashboard New Session button), and the typed-command rollover path `initSessionState` → `commitReplySessionInitialization`, plus the internal self-heal path `persistSessionResetLifecycle`.
- The referenced-sessions guard snapshot is taken **inside the locked store mutator** (`referencedSessionIdsAtSwap`), closing a race where an unlocked re-read after two await points could see a concurrent writer's row and silently skip the tombstone.
- **External trajectory directories** (`OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR`): the pair is tombstoned in place only under proven ownership (registry-owned, or the session's own pointer file names the target); unproven files in an operator-configured directory are left untouched. The retention sweep follows tombstone directories, so aging works there too.
- **No new retention code.** Tombstoned trajectories reuse the existing `.reset.<ts>` / `.deleted.<ts>` suffix conventions and age out with the existing archived-transcript sweep.

## Why rename instead of delete on reset

No merged commit or confirmed-maintainer comment currently states reset-vs-trajectory policy explicitly, but the record strongly and repeatedly converges on one answer: reset must preserve trajectory records via rename/archive, never delete them outright. This is proposed directly in [#90707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90707) (with a concrete forensics-loss incident as motivation), implemented the same way in the still-open [#94593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593) (after two prior closed-unmerged attempts at the identical shape, [#93319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93319) and [#94895](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94895)), echoed by the broader "never `rm` a session file, only move/rename" position in [#56609](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/56609), and most directly, flagged as a P1 blocker on this very branch by the automated reviewer, which asked explicitly to "preserve or archive pre-reset trajectories instead of deleting them." This PR's tombstone-rename on the runner-driven `/reset` path is our attempt to satisfy that converging intent without waiting on #94593 to land, since the two changes touch adjacent but distinct code paths (delete-lifecycle cleanup vs. the shared reset-archive helper) and reconciling them is better done as a maintainer-guided follow-up than by blocking this fix on an unrelated open PR.

## Evidence

Test gates on the final head: `session-accessor.test.ts` 73/73, `session.test.ts` 143/143, adjacent lifecycle suites 24/24 (240 total), typecheck (`tsgo:core` + `tsgo:core:test`) clean, oxlint/oxfmt clean. Every fix commit is red-proven: the concurrent-writer race test and the entry-level typed-`/reset` test (entering through `initSessionState`, not the inner function) each fail against the pre-fix code exactly as observed live and pass after.

Live validation on a v2026.6.10 production deployment (session ids redacted):

```
typed /reset:
  <sid-A>.jsonl.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z
  <sid-A>.trajectory.jsonl.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z
  <sid-A>.trajectory-path.json.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z

dashboard delete: same trio shape with .deleted.<ts>, session key removed, clean re-mint on next message

typed /new with OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR set (trajectory lives outside the sessions dir):
  sessions dir:  <sid-B>.jsonl.reset.<ts>  +  <sid-B>.trajectory-path.json.reset.<ts>
  external dir:  <sid-B>.jsonl.reset.<ts>   (renamed in place, same timestamp)
```

## Scope notes

- `applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation` (the batched background-maintenance mutation used by the session reaper, cleanup service, and heartbeat runner) is deliberately not touched: its removed-session cleanup already routes through the trajectory-coupled maintenance helpers, and unreferenced pairs are reclaimed by the age-based prune, which is the correct model for background reaping (no user action to timestamp-couple to).
- [#94593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593) partially overlaps on intent (reset-time preservation) but implements it in the shared reset-archive helper; this PR covers the delete lifecycle and the typed-command rollover door. If #94593 lands first we are happy to rebase and drop any overlap, and vice versa.

## User Impact

Deleting or resetting a session, from any surface, now leaves a complete archived trio with one shared timestamp instead of orphaned or destroyed trajectory files. Post-incident forensics of tool calls survives resets. Existing retention behavior and bounds are unchanged.

target.title: fix(clawrouter): guard usage snapshot fetch against SSRF redirects
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClawRouter usage snapshot fetches used an unguarded `fetch` against an operator-configured `baseUrl`. A malicious or compromised usage endpoint could redirect the request onto a private/internal address, and the call path skipped the shared SSRF guard already used for ClawRouter live catalog discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route `fetchClawRouterUsage` through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` the same way live catalog discovery does: the guard owns production transport (no caller `fetchImpl`), so DNS pinning cannot be overwritten by provider usage proxy wrappers. Tests inject an optional `fetchGuard` seam; production callers no longer pass `ctx.fetchFn`.

## User Impact

ClawRouter `/usage` status no longer follows redirects from the configured host into private/internal networks. Healthy public ClawRouter usage endpoints continue to work.

## Evidence

### Unit + controlled-server production-transport proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > maps the managed monthly budget and usage totals 151ms
 ✓ ... > shows aggregate usage for an unmetered key 2ms
 ✓ ... > does not expose an upstream error body 1ms
 ✓ ... > bounds successful usage response bodies 17ms
 ✓ ... > fetches usage through the production SSRF-guarded transport 326ms
 ✓ ... > blocks private-network redirects on the production transport path 55ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.62s
```

The last two cases exercise production `fetchClawRouterUsage` with no injected fetch/guard: a real `node:http` loopback server for healthy usage, and a `302` to `http://10.0.0.1:9/v1/usage` that the shared guard rejects before a second hop.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** ClawRouter usage fetches no longer follow redirects from the configured host onto private/internal targets, and production transport stays under the shared SSRF guard's dispatcher.
- **Canonical reachability path:** provider usage snapshot → `fetchUsageSnapshot` in `extensions/clawrouter/index.ts` → `fetchClawRouterUsage` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` (no `fetchImpl`).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime SSRF guard; controlled `node:http` server on loopback; private redirect target.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + `ssrfPolicyFromHttpBaseUrlAllowedHostname` already used by ClawRouter live catalog discovery; same guard-owned transport shape as catalog (no provider usage proxy as `fetchImpl`).
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with real HTTP listeners.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ |extensions| extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts > ClawRouter usage > fetches usage through the production SSRF-guarded transport 326ms
 ✓ |extensions| extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts > ClawRouter usage > blocks private-network redirects on the production transport path 55ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.62s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Healthy usage returns the mapped snapshot over the guard-owned transport; private-network redirect rejects with a blocked/private/internal error and the controlled server sees only the first hop.
- **What was not tested:** Live ClawRouter cloud `/v1/usage` against a real proxy key; Gateway status UI end-to-end; HTTP_PROXY-managed usage routing (usage now matches catalog and uses guard-owned direct transport rather than `resolveProxyFetchFromEnv` as `fetchImpl`).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. Only the ClawRouter usage HTTP transport gains the shared SSRF guard with guard-owned dispatcher. Successful responses from the configured host are unchanged; operator-configured private base URLs remain allowed when that hostname is the configured endpoint (same policy shape as catalog discovery). Usage snapshot fetching no longer routes through the provider usage proxy fetch wrapper, matching catalog discovery.

target.title: fix: webChat scrollback history is too limited — older assistant replies and tool outputs disappear when scrolling…
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Fixes an issue where users paginating session history could never reach a compaction marker that the full history reader included before the active transcript branch.**
- **Affected surface / workflow:** Gateway/session history JSONL indexing and offset pagination used by history consumers.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The full reader preserves the nearest compaction record before an explicitly selected active branch, but the byte-offset transcript index built its active view from branch nodes only. Pagination therefore indexed three visible rows where the full reader exposed four.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** `totalMessages` and message `seq` values were shifted, and no offset could retrieve the compaction boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** One shared transcript-tree selector now owns active-branch plus nearest-preceding-compaction selection, and both the full/bounded filesystem reader and byte-offset index consume it before assigning sequence numbers or serving pages.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** Counts, sequence metadata, identity lookups, and pages all derive from the transcript index; correcting its active-entry selection restores one consistent visible-history invariant rather than patching pagination output downstream.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** `src/config/sessions/transcript-tree.ts` owns active transcript selection for all filesystem readers. It selects the normalized active path and nearest preceding compaction once; `session-utils.fs.ts` and `session-transcript-index.fs.ts` only adapt their record wrappers to that canonical helper.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** No protocol/schema/UI changes, no new cursor semantics, and no change to linear transcripts or all-entry identity lookup.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** This is an additive correction to existing history contents and metadata. Open PR #87111 adds broader WebChat cursor pagination and active-branch indexing work; this PR is intentionally separate and narrower because its current implementation does not preserve the pre-branch compaction row in the index. If #87111 lands, this invariant should be retained during integration.
- **Related open PR scan:** #87111 was inspected at current head `394564241690`; it implements cursor/UI pagination but its active index path still selects only branch nodes, so it does not cover the compaction-before-active-branch edge case. Other related PRs surfaced by the issue workflow do not make current `main` behavior equivalent to this fix.
- **Out of scope:** WebChat controls, Gateway protocol fields, page-size policy, display projection, imported CLI history, and cursor design remain owned by #87111 or later work.
- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: session-state` and `merge-risk: availability`.
- **Risk explanation:** The transcript index is shared by count, full async, and paginated history readers, so changing active-entry selection can affect visible history metadata. The change only restores the nearest compaction row already exposed by the synchronous full reader and leaves branch-message filtering unchanged.
- **Why acceptable:** The fix makes all production readers agree on one existing visible-history invariant, is covered with a real branched JSONL fixture, and changes no API, schema, persistence format, or fallback behavior.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Page all the way back to the compaction marker and observe `totalMessages`/`seq` values matching full history for the same JSONL transcript.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** Active-branch filtering still excludes abandoned and side-branch messages; only the already-visible compaction boundary is restored to the indexed view.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** No browser UI proof was needed because this fix is below the UI/protocol layer. The production filesystem full and paginated readers were exercised directly against the same real JSONL file.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash, Node 22.17.0, pnpm 11.2.2. The branch was synced through the required daily-fix `sync-main` flow after drift analysis found a real merge conflict and dependency-file changes across 212 upstream commits.
- **Commands run after this patch:** focused `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts`; exact formerly failing `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`; a production-path TypeScript script calling `readSessionMessages` and `readSessionMessagesPageWithStatsAsync` against one on-disk JSONL; `git diff --check`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** write one branched session JSONL containing an abandoned branch, a compaction marker, the selected active branch, a side branch, and a leaf selector; call the production full reader once; then call the production paginated reader with `maxMessages=1` at offsets 0 through 4; compare visible rows, `totalMessages`, and `seq` values.
- **Observed result after fix:** Before the fix, full history returned 4 rows with compaction `seq=1`, while pagination reported `totalMessages=3`, shifted active rows to `seq=1..3`, and could not retrieve compaction at any offset. On the synced fixed head, pagination reports `totalMessages=4`; offsets 0/1/2 return active rows at `seq=4/3/2`; offset 3 returns compaction `seq=1`; offset 4 is empty. Gateway coverage passed 388/388. The old CI failure was unrelated to this PR, and the exact doctor-health suite now passes 91/91.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** `RF-001` waiting-on-author is addressed by this update. `RF-002` and `RF-005` fixed — full/bounded and indexed readers now use one canonical selector in `transcript-tree.ts`. `RF-003` fixed — the closing footer was replaced with a non-closing related-work reference. `RF-004` documented — #87111 integration must retain this shared selector and regression invariant. `RF-006` passed — Gateway suite 388/388. `RF-007` passed — `git diff --check` is clean.
- **Target regression test:** the branched real-JSONL case in `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts`.
- **Regression scenario:** compaction immediately precedes the selected active branch while abandoned and side-branch messages remain excluded.
- **Why this test is a guardrail:** it fails if compaction disappears again, if offsets cannot reach it, or if `totalMessages`/`seq` diverge between full and paginated readers.
- **Regression guardrail:** `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts` locks a branched real-JSONL scenario where compaction immediately precedes the selected active branch; it is the smallest reliable guard because it simultaneously verifies active-branch filtering, compaction reachability, offsets, `totalMessages`, and sequence assignment through the production reader.
- **Unavailable environment disclosure:** the workflow reports no local Gateway daemon proof capability. A daemon/browser is not part of this filesystem-reader boundary; instead, the actual production full and paginated reader functions were executed against a real on-disk JSONL, with exact output included above.
- **Patch quality notes:** Two-file focused change; no fallback, protocol expansion, generated files, dependencies, or lockfile changes.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for this narrow invariant; production reader proof and regression coverage agree.

Related to #92317; this PR restores the compaction/index invariant, while broader WebChat cursor and older-history loading remains tracked separately.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA Lab Telegram live progress output can contain malformed text when a detail message has emoji at the 240-character truncation boundary.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Browser action requests could accept loose coordinate numbers for `clickCoords`, such as hexadecimal or exponent-form strings, when users or tools submit direct coordinate clicks through the browser `/act` workflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

`clickCoords` now uses one browser-owned decimal-only finite coordinate parser from both the CLI and the `/act` route before dispatch, matching the Browser CLI contract that allows fractional CSS-pixel coordinates while rejecting non-decimal numeric syntax. This is an owner-local browser route/CLI normalization fix only; it does not add config, compatibility aliases, or provider behavior.

## User Impact

Browser action callers get consistent validation for coordinate clicks: decimal and fractional coordinates continue to work, while hexadecimal and exponent-form strings are rejected before malformed coordinate clicks are dispatched.

Fixes MS Teams group/channel file sends that could hang indefinitely when SharePoint upload, sharing-link creation, chat-member lookup, or drive-item metadata requests stalled before headers or while reading response bodies.

The affected SharePoint/Graph calls now use an aborting timeout around the full fetch lifecycle, including response body reads. The timeout helper lives in `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts`, the existing MS Teams timeout owner.

target.title: fix(agents): distinguish z.ai code 1305 content rejection from generic overload
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: z.ai Coding Plan endpoint returns HTTP 429 with code 1305 deterministically when the system prompt contains "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw". The current error classifier treats all 1305 responses as generic overload, showing "The AI service is temporarily overloaded" to users — which is misleading for the content-rejection case.

**Solution**: Add a `ZAI_CODE_1305_RE` pattern to detect `{"code":1305,...}` or `{"code":"1305",...}` (quoted or unquoted) in the raw error message and surface a more specific diagnostic before falling back to the generic overload message. The `classifyFailoverReason` hook in the z.ai plugin ensures code 1305 is classified as "overloaded" (provider-scoped), preventing misclassification by the generic rate-limit pattern.

**What changed**: 
- `sanitize-user-facing-text.ts`: Updated `ZAI_CODE_1305_RE` regex constant to match both `"code":1305` (unquoted number) and `"code":"1305"` (quoted string) JSON values; new check in `formatRateLimitOrOverloadedErrorCopy` that runs before `isOverloadedErrorMessage` and returns a neutral diagnostic for z.ai 1305 errors: "transient overload or a provider-side content restriction — try again later or with a different model."
- `extensions/zai/index.ts`: Added `classifyFailoverReason` hook that explicitly classifies z.ai code 1305 as "overloaded" (provider-scoped, prevents generic rate-limit classification from bypassing the diagnostic check)
- `failover-matches.test.ts`, `formatassistanterrortext.test.ts`: Updated tests to expect the new diagnostic message

**What did NOT change**:
- The `rate_limit` failover classification is preserved — backoff and fallback continue working
- Non-1305 overload errors return the original "overloaded" message unchanged
- Zhipu GLM `[1305]` format is not affected (doesn't match the JSON key pattern)

**Fixes**: #103529

## What Problem This Solves

Users onboarding a valid z.ai Coding Plan key successfully, but every chat turn fails with a misleading "overloaded" error. The real cause — the system prompt signature line triggering a provider-side content filter — is invisible. Users waste time checking quota, retrying, or switching API keys when the issue is the system prompt content.

## Root Cause

z.ai's Coding Plan endpoint returns HTTP 429 with `{"error":{"code":"1305","message":"The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later."}}` when the system message contains "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw". This behavior is a **deterministic function of the system prompt content**, not a transient overload. Removing or altering that one line produces a 200 response.

The error classifier in `sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` matched the "overloaded" keyword in the response body and returned the generic overload message, which is incorrect for this scenario.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Error message for z.ai code 1305 now mentions possible content restriction instead of generic overload

**Real environment tested**: Node 24, macOS, tsx 4.19, vitest 4.1.9

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Direct call to `formatRateLimitOrOverloadedErrorCopy` (production function) via tsx — covering canonical payload, backward-compatible format, and non-1305 fallthrough.

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal
$ node --import tsx zai-1305-evidence.ts
=== Part 1: Canonical payload ===
Input: {"error":{"code":"1305","message":"The service may be temporarily..."}}
Output: ⚠️ Provider returned code 1305. This can be a transient overload
or a provider-side content restriction — try again later or with a
different model.

=== Part 2: Backward compatible ===
Input: {"code":1305,"message":"..."}
Output: ⚠️ Provider returned code 1305. [same diagnostic]

=== Part 3: Non-1305 fallthrough ===
Generic overload: "The AI service is temporarily overloaded." ← unchanged
Rate limit with retry: "⚠️ rate limit: service overloaded..." ← preserved
Zhipu GLM [1305]: undefined ← not affected
Non-z.ai 429: "⚠️ API rate limit reached." ← passes through
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The diagnostic is more neutral — it covers both overload and content-rejection scenarios without misleading users toward "system prompt" guidance they cannot act on. Provider-scoping through the z.ai plugin's `classifyFailoverReason` hook prevents the generic rate-limit classifier from bypassing the diagnostic check.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end with a real z.ai API key (L3 full gateway run). The original issue (#103529) provides curl-level reproduction. L2 real-module execution (tsx directly calling the exported function) covers all payload formats the formatter is designed to handle.

## Tests and validation

**Exact steps or command run**: vitest run (32 + 90 + 15 tests)

**Test output**:
```terminal
✓ failover-matches.test.ts: 32 passed
✓ formatassistanterrortext.test.ts: 90 passed
✓ extensions/zai/index.test.ts: 15 passed
Total: 137 passed
```

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Provider-scoped: z.ai plugin's classifyFailoverReason hook ensures code 1305 is only handled within z.ai provider context
- [x] Neutral diagnostic: "transient overload or content restriction" handles both scenarios without speculation
- [x] No change to failover/fallback behavior (rate_limit/overloaded classification preserved)
- [x] All 137 unit tests pass
- [x] 26 insertions, 8 deletions — within the Diamond Lobster 100-line limit

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.body:
## Summary

- add an in-app, read-only artifact viewer for code, text, Markdown, PDF, DOCX, and uploaded HTML files
- replace document download-only cards with an accessible open action while preserving downloads and existing image/audio/video behavior
- add desktop side-pane and mobile full-screen presentation with focus restoration, Escape handling, loading states, and pane-local fallbacks
- classify using stored upload MIME metadata plus the original filename because unsafe upload types are served as `application/octet-stream`
- add the viewer dependencies, embedded production assets, documentation, and browser coverage

## Viewer behavior

- code and text render as inert escaped source; known languages up to 256 KiB are highlighted in a terminable worker, while larger files use escaped plain-text fallback
- Markdown supports sanitized preview and source modes through the existing `marked` and DOMPurify pipeline
- PDF supports one-page-at-a-time navigation, page counts, and zoom using the existing `pdfjs-dist` integration
- DOCX converts semantically in-browser with Mammoth and sanitizes the resulting HTML
- uploaded HTML is sanitized, placed in an empty-sandbox `iframe.srcdoc`, and constrained by a CSP that permits only inline styles and local `data:`/`blob:` assets
- unsupported files show metadata and a download fallback without execution

## Safety contract

- text, code, Markdown, and HTML previews are limited to 2 MiB
- syntax highlighting is isolated from the UI thread in a terminable worker with a 2-second timeout and 2 MiB output cap; files above 256 KiB remain escaped source without syntax parsing
- DOCX conversion is limited to 16 MiB; PDF preview uses the existing 64 MiB upload ceiling
- previews use same-origin authenticated fetches, abort on close/switch, and release worker/PDF resources
- HTML scripts, forms, frames, external links/resources, and network-bearing CSS references are removed before rendering; server download headers and CSP are unchanged
- v1 is read-only and does not add artifact storage, editing, collaboration, or CRDT state
- no database, OpenAPI, SDK, or public transport contract changes

## Verification

- `pnpm check`
- `pnpm coverage` — 86.5% total Go coverage
- `pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/artifact-viewer.spec.ts` — 5 passed, covering classification, worker highlighting, near-limit escaped fallback and cancellation, Markdown source/preview, PDF page/zoom, bounded DOCX conversion, hostile-HTML isolation, oversized/malformed fallbacks, mobile sizing, and `message.updated`
- `CAPTURE_ARTIFACT_PROOF=1 pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/artifact-viewer.spec.ts -g "opens safe code"` — 1 passed and produced live HTML-isolation diagnostics
- production web/SDK build and embedded asset refresh completed through the E2E web server
- browser visual inspection completed for the desktop side pane, mobile full-screen layout, and HTML-isolation diagnostic capture

## Real behavior proof

These captures come from the local OpenClaw → ClickClack delivery path and the running viewer.

### Uploaded HTML isolation

The hostile fixture attempts script execution, form submission, nested framing, external navigation, image loading, stylesheet import, and CSS URL loading. Browser-observed diagnostics show an empty sandbox token list, an absent script marker, zero requests to the sentinel host, no scripts/forms/frames in the preview DOM, and stripped external URL references.

![Uploaded HTML isolation with live browser diagnostics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/a2460a156d7165e01322dc71d37f85996f3656c0/docs/proof/artifact-viewer-html-isolation.png)

Reproduction details: [`docs/artifact-viewer-security-proof.md`](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/blob/a2460a156d7165e01322dc71d37f85996f3656c0/docs/artifact-viewer-security-proof.md)

### Behavior while testing PR

![Markdown preview side pane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/3d94e34/docs/proof/artifact-viewer-markdown-preview.png)

![Markdown source side pane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/3d94e34/docs/proof/artifact-viewer-markdown-source.png)

### Current behavior before merging PR

![OpenClaw-delivered ClickClack attachment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/3d94e34/docs/proof/openclaw-clickclack-attachment.png)

![Download control behavior](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/3d94e34/docs/proof/openclaw-download-permission.png)

## Out of scope

- OpenClaw `sendMedia` delivery remains a separate companion PR
- collaborative Markdown, mutable uploads, revisioned artifacts, and Jot/CRDT storage remain follow-up work
